mainTopic: Which תנא our משנה follows on writing and signing לשמה, and whether the opinions in the משנה reflect the two reasons for 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'
overview: Our משנה has the messenger say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם', which suggests that both the writing and the signing of a גט must be לשמה. The גמרא finishes showing that רבי מאיר cannot be the author, because רב נחמן reports that רבי מאיר accepts a גט found in the garbage. It rejects the defense that this is only Torah law. It then explains the משנה as רבי אלעזר, who requires proper signing whenever witnesses do sign, and supports this with רבי אבא. רב אשי says instead that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the גמרא explains why it tried רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר first. Next, the גמרא looks at רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, who require the declaration even for towns right next to ארץ ישראל. It asks whether their argument with the תנא קמא matches the two reasons for the declaration: lack of experts in לשמה, or lack of witnesses to confirm the גט. It answers that רבה and רבא can each explain all three opinions with his own reason. Finally, it turns to the חכמים, who add 'the one who takes it overseas', and begins a similar suggestion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge from רב נחמן's report about רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב נחמן's quote: a גט found in the garbage, then signed and given, is valid according to רבי מאיר. So רבי מאיר does not need the writing to be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and he signed it and gave it to her, it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote it began just before this point. רב נחמן reported that according to רבי מאיר, a husband who found a written גט in the garbage, signed it and gave it to his wife has a valid גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר accepts a גט that was never written for this woman, he clearly does not need the כתיבה to be לשמה. That clashes with our משנה, which cares about 'בפני נכתב'. So the משנה cannot easily follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: for her sake, done specifically for this woman

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the tail end of a quote. The quote opens with 'אמר רב נחמן אומר היה רבי מאיר אפילו מצאו באשפה', which comes right before this point.

phrases.english: and he signed it and gave it to her, it is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began right before this point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that our משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר accepts a גט that was not written לשמה, yet our משנה cares about the writing.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that רב נחמן was only speaking about Torah law
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say רב נחמן only described the Torah law, and that by rabbinic law רבי מאיר does need the writing to be לשמה. The גמרא rejects this because רב נחמן would then have said 'דבר תורה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we teach רב נחמן's statement as Torah law, then he should have said 'רבי מאיר used to say: by Torah law'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to save רבי מאיר and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested defense is that רבי מאיר permits the garbage גט only on the Torah level, while by rabbinic law רבי מאיר himself still requires the writing to be לשמה, which would fit our משנה. The גמרא rejects it from the wording. If that were the point, רב נחמן should have said 'by Torah law', and he did not.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (a possible answer about to be rejected)

phrases.english: And if you would say
we teach it as Torah law,
phrases.notes: The suggestion is that by rabbinic law רבי מאיר would still require the writing to be for her sake.

phrases.english: if so,

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּבַר תּוֹרָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he should have said: 'Rabbi Meir would say: by Torah law'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אֲנַן מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא קָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible defense against the challenge in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רב נחמן's statement is limited to Torah law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן's wording has no 'דבר תורה', which it would need if that limit were intended.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר when there are witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רבי מאיר and says the משנה follows רבי אלעזר after all. רבי אלעזר does not need signatures only when the גט has no witnesses at all. If witnesses do sign, their signing must be לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really it is רבי אלעזר. When does רבי אלעזר not require signing? When there are no witnesses at all. When there are witnesses, he does require it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, with a limit on how far his view goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the problem with רבי אלעזר was that he says the delivery witnesses (עדי מסירה) are what count, so signing should not matter. Now the גמרא narrows his view. A גט with no witness signatures at all is fine, but if witnesses did sign, their signing must be done properly, meaning לשמה. So our משנה can require both 'נכתב' and 'נחתם' and still follow רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: witnesses to the handing over of the גט

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר still holds that the delivery witnesses are what make the גט work. The point here is only that if there are signing witnesses, their signing cannot be done improperly.

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לָא בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חֲתִימָה –
phrases.english: and when does Rabbi Elazar not require signing?
Where there are no witnesses at all;
where there are witnesses, he does require it.
phrases.notes: He means the witnesses' signing must be for her sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי מאיר approach after steps 1 and 2 and answers with רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing a תנא's view to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר never cares about signing, so the משנה cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר requires proper signing whenever witnesses actually sign, so the משנה fits him.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אבא: a גט with built-in forgery is invalid even for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says רבי אלעזר agrees that a גט whose flaw is inside the document itself is invalid. This supports the idea that improper signatures ruin the גט even for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבא said: רבי אלעזר agrees that a document forged from within is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the limit it just put on רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'מזויף מתוכו' is a document whose own contents show it is flawed, such as one signed by unfit witnesses. Even רבי אלעזר, who relies on the delivery witnesses, rules it invalid. So once witnesses sign, their signatures must be proper, and that fits a requirement that they sign לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: a document forged from within, whose flaw shows from the document itself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, a גט can work with no signing witnesses. But if it has signatures, they must be proper, so the משנה's 'בפני נחתם' fits him.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abba said:
Rabbi Elazar agrees about a document forged from within,
phrases.notes: A document whose flaw shows from the document itself, like one signed by witnesses who are not fit to sign.

phrases.english: that it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּמְזוּיָּיף מִתּוֹכוֹ
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר requires proper signing when witnesses do sign
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבא's statement about מזויף מתוכו

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה requires both the writing and the signing to be done on something detached from the ground, which shows he cares about both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, as we learned: רבי יהודה invalidates the גט unless both its writing and its signing are on something detached.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to explain the משנה, using a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a later משנה, רבי יהודה requires both the כתיבה and the חתימה to be done on a detached object. That shows he treats both writing and signing as important acts of the גט. So he would also require both to be לשמה, which matches our משנה's 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a later משנה in גיטין, on דף כא עמוד ב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda invalidates it,
unless its writing and its signing are on something detached.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from the רבי אלעזר answer in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the משנה with a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow רבי מאיר or רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי יהודה, who treats both writing and signing as key acts of the גט.

steps.title: Why not say רבי יהודה from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it did not explain the משנה as רבי יהודה from the beginning, since his view is stated openly in a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at first, what was the reason we did not explain it according to רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about its own path. It is setting up an explanation of why רבי יהודה was not the first choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view is stated plainly in a משנה, so he seems like the obvious answer. The question suggests there must be some reason the גמרא first worked so hard with רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: we explain it as, we set it according to

phrases.english: And at first, what is the reason
we did not explain it according to Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מוֹקְמִינַן לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the answer from step 5 was not given first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the גמרא first avoided placing the משנה with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why we first tried רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that it tried רבי מאיר first because an unnamed משנה follows him. It tried רבי אלעזר because the הלכה follows him in גיטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We try to explain the משנה as רבי מאיר, because an unnamed משנה is usually רבי מאיר. We try to explain it as רבי אלעזר, because we hold the הלכה follows him in matters of גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from Step 6. It explains why it did not start with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view fit easily, but the גמרא had good reasons to try the other two first. An unnamed משנה is normally רבי מאיר's. The הלכה in גיטין follows רבי אלעזר. So it made sense to try to fit the משנה to one of them before turning to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: We go looking for, we try hard to fit
An unnamed משנה, one that gives no author
We hold as an established rule

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא prefers to explain a משנה as רבי מאיר, since an unnamed משנה follows him, or as רבי אלעזר, since the הלכה follows him in גיטין. That is why רב אשי's answer with רבי יהודה came last.

phrases.english: We seek to explain it as Rabbi Meir,
since an unnamed Mishnah is Rabbi Meir;
we seek to explain it as Rabbi Elazar,
since we hold the halacha follows him in bills of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6, which asked why the גמרא did not start with רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the גמרא did not use רבי יהודה from the start.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It preferred רבי מאיר, since an unnamed משנה follows him, and רבי אלעזר, since the הלכה follows him in גיטין.

steps.title: The משנה about places near ארץ ישראל, and אביי's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבן גמליאל says that even someone bringing a גט from רקם or חגר must make the declaration. רבי אליעזר says the same even from כפר לודים to לוד. אביי explains that these are towns near ארץ ישראל and surrounded by its border.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבן גמליאל says that even one who brings a גט from רקם or from חגר must say the declaration. רבי אליעזר says: even one who brings it from the village of לודים to לוד. And אביי said: we are dealing with towns that are near ארץ ישראל and enclosed inside its border.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new discussion. It quotes a piece of the משנה and אביי's explanation of it, to set up a question coming soon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main rule is that someone bringing a גט from outside ארץ ישראל must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר add places that are very close to ארץ ישראל. אביי explains that these towns are not part of ארץ ישראל, but they are next to it and surrounded by its border.

keyTerms.meaning: Two places at the edge of ארץ ישראל
A village close to the city of לוד

phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמֵּבִיא מִן הָרְקָם וּמִן הַחֶגֶר.
phrases.english: Even one who brings a get from Rekem or from Ḥeger.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even from the village of Ludim to Lod.
And Abaye said:
With towns that are near Eretz Yisrael
and enclosed within the border of Eretz Yisrael we are dealing,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of which תנא the משנה follows. Starts a new look at the משנה, using its added places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר require the declaration even for towns right next to ארץ ישראל and surrounded by its border.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה shows how close these places are
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says he saw the place himself. The distance was like the short trip from בי כובי to פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said: I myself saw that place, and it was like the distance from בי כובי to פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה adds an eyewitness report showing how short the distance is. This finishes the setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These places are extremely close to ארץ ישראל. That makes it surprising that anyone would require the declaration there. It also makes clear that the תנא קמא, who does not mention these places, does not require it.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Babylonian city with a yeshiva

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
I myself saw that place,
and it was like from Bei Kuvei to Pumbedita.
phrases.notes: These two Babylonian places were very close, so this was a short distance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי הָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the actual distance to אביי's description of the places in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The distance from כפר לודים to לוד is very short, like from בי כובי to פומבדיתא.

steps.title: Is the argument in the משנה about the two reasons for the declaration?
steps.stepSummary: From this, the תנא קמא does not require the declaration for these nearby places. The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא holds the reason is lack of experts in writing לשמה, and these people are experts. רבן גמליאל holds the reason is lack of witnesses to confirm the גט, and these people are also not easy to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that the תנא קמא holds the declaration is not needed for these places. Is it not that they argue about this? One holds the reason is that people are not experts in writing לשמה, and these people are learned. The other holds the reason is that witnesses are not available to confirm the גט, and these people are also not easy to find.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה. It then asks whether the argument between the תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל is really the same as the two reasons for the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason for the declaration is the lack of experts in writing לשמה, nearby towns do not need it, since their people know the laws. If the reason is that witnesses cannot easily be found to confirm the גט, even nearby towns across the border need it. This would turn the two reasons into an argument between תנאים, which the גמרא will examine next.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Experts in writing the גט for this specific woman
To confirm it, to authenticate the signatures

steps.confusionAlert: The first מר here is the תנא קמא (the reason is לשמה), and the second מר is רבן גמליאל (the reason is confirming the גט). Do not mix them up: the side that cares about לשמה is the side that does not require the declaration in these nearby towns.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this suggestion holds, each of the two reasons for 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' would match only one side of a dispute in the משנה. That would mean neither reason fits the whole משנה.

phrases.english: This implies that the first tanna holds
these do not need it;
What, is it not about this that they argue?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ,
phrases.english: That one Sage holds: because they are not experts in writing it for her sake,
phrases.notes: This Sage is the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: and these people are learned;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ,
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: because there are no witnesses available to confirm it,
and these people are also not commonly available?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר הָנֵי לָא צְרִיךְ; מַאי, לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the places from Step 8 and their closeness from Step 9 to infer the תנא קמא's view and suggest what the argument is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between the תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל the same as the two reasons for the declaration (לשמה or confirming the גט)?
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a single reason for 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם' fits the whole משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תנא קמא follows the לשמה reason and רבן גמליאל follows the confirming reason, then each reason matches only one side of the משנה's dispute.

steps.title: No proof: each אמורא can explain the משנה his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 10. It says both רבה and רבא can fit the whole משנה into their own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רבה explains the משנה according to his reasoning, and רבא explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to the idea that the תנאים argue about רבה's and רבא's reasons. It is setting up two full explanations, one for רבה and one for רבא, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 tried to show that the argument between רבה and רבא is really an older argument between תנאים. The גמרא now says this does not follow. Each אמורא can read all the opinions in the משנה as agreeing with his own basic reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains or resolves (here, fits the משנה into his view)

phrases.english: No; Rabba explains [the mishna] according to his reasoning,
and Rava explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; רַבָּה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, וְרָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 10 that the משנה shows a dispute among תנאים about the basic reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that the תנאים argue about רבה's and רבא's reasons. It does not reject either reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read so that all three תנאים agree on one basic reason, either רבה's or רבא's. So it does not prove they argue about the reason.

steps.title: How רבה explains all three opinions
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, everyone agrees the reason is that people outside ארץ ישראל are not experts in לשמה. The argument is only about which nearby places are considered learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה explains it his way. Everyone agrees the reason is that people are not experts in writing a גט לשמה. They disagree about this: the תנא קמא holds that places near ארץ ישראל are learned. רבן גמליאל comes to say that places enclosed inside the border are learned, but places that are only nearby are not. רבי אליעזר comes to say that even the enclosed places are not treated as learned, so that you do not start making distinctions among places outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבה reads the משנה. All three תנאים use his reason about experts in לשמה, and they argue only about where people are learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא is the most lenient: even nearby places know the rule. רבן גמליאל is stricter: only places enclosed by the border know it. רבי אליעזר is strictest: even enclosed places get the full rule of outside ארץ ישראל, because the חכמים did not want to divide up places outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts, people who know the rule well
Places enclosed inside the border of ארץ ישראל
They are learned (they know the rule)
Lands overseas, meaning outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר says the people of enclosed towns really do not know the rule. He says the חכמים gave all places outside ארץ ישראל one rule, so we do not make distinctions.

phrases.english: Rabba explains according to his reasoning:
that everyone agrees
[the reason is] because they are not experts in [writing] for her sake,
and here they disagree about this:
the first tanna holds:
these [towns], since they are nearby,
are certainly learned [in the rule];
and Rabban Gamliel came to say:
enclosed [towns] are learned,
phrases.notes: Enclosed means surrounded by the border of ארץ ישראל, like אביי explained in step 8.

phrases.english: [towns that are only] nearby are not learned;
and Rabbi Eliezer came to say:
enclosed [towns] also are not [treated as learned],
so that you should not make distinctions among lands overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first half of the rejection in step 11: how רבה fits all three opinions into his reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the dispute: all agree on the basic reason, and they argue only about which places it applies to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבן גמליאל seemed to argue about the basic reason, experts in לשמה against available witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבה, all agree the reason is lack of experts in לשמה. The argument is whether nearby or enclosed towns count as learned.

steps.title: How רבא explains all three opinions
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, everyone agrees the reason is that witnesses to confirm the גט are hard to find. The argument is only about which nearby places count as having witnesses easily available.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explains it his way. Everyone agrees the reason is that witnesses are not easily found to confirm the גט. The תנא קמא holds that places near ארץ ישראל are frequently available. רבן גמליאל comes to say that places enclosed inside the border are frequently available, but places that are only nearby are not. רבי אליעזר comes to say that even the enclosed places are not, so that you do not start making distinctions among places outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows that רבא can read the משנה the same way, using his own reason about witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure matches רבה's reading exactly. Only the reason changes: 'are they learned?' becomes 'are witnesses easy to find?'. Since both readings work, the משנה cannot prove which reason is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: To confirm it (to verify the signatures on the גט)
They are frequently found or available

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about רקם, חגר, and כפר לודים does not decide between רבה and רבא. Each can explain all three תנאים using his own reason. In both readings, the argument is only about which places near ארץ ישראל get the rule of outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rava explains according to his reasoning:
that everyone agrees
[the reason is] because witnesses are not available to confirm it;
and the first tanna holds:
these [towns], since they are nearby,
are certainly frequently available;
phrases.notes: He means people from these towns often come to ארץ ישראל, so witnesses who know the signatures can be found.

phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel came to say:
enclosed [towns] are frequently available,
[towns that are only] nearby are not frequently available;
and Rabbi Eliezer came to say:
enclosed [towns] also are not [treated as available],
so that you should not make distinctions among lands overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֵדִים מְצוּיִין לְקַיְּימוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 12. It completes the rejection in step 11 by showing that רבא can also explain the whole משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel re-reading: the same pattern of dispute, built on רבא's reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's reason seemed to match רבן גמליאל only, not the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, all agree the reason is that witnesses are hard to find. The argument is whether nearby or enclosed towns count as places where witnesses are frequently available.

steps.title: Quoting the view of the Sages in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה: the declaration is needed for one who brings a גט from overseas, and also for one who takes a גט overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: The חכמים say that no one needs to say "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence" except the person who brings a גט from overseas and the person who takes one there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה, the opinion of the חכמים. It is setting up the next move, where it will draw a conclusion from this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the declaration applies in two directions: bringing a גט into ארץ ישראל from overseas, and taking a גט out of ארץ ישראל to overseas. The word מוליך, 'the one who takes it there', is the new detail the גמרא will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the group opinion in the משנה
One who carries a גט from ארץ ישראל to overseas

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה:
And the Sages say:
One does not need to say
"It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,"
except the one who brings it from overseas
and the one who takes it there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the argument of רבן גמליאל according to both רבה and רבא, the גמרא turns to another line of the משנה to test the two reasons again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the declaration is needed both for one who brings a גט from overseas and for one who takes a גט overseas.

steps.title: Inferring that the first opinion does not require it for taking a get overseas
steps.stepSummary: Because the חכמים had to add 'the one who takes it there', the תנא קמא must hold that someone taking a גט overseas does not need the declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that the תנא קמא holds that the person who takes a גט overseas does not need to say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the words of the חכמים. If they added the case of taking a גט overseas, the תנא קמא must not have required the declaration in that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה only spoke about someone bringing a גט from overseas. The חכמים adding מוליך shows there is a real argument, and the argument is about the person who takes a גט overseas. This sets up the question of what reason lies behind that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: This shows that the first opinion holds
the one who takes it there does not need to say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the חכמים quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא does not require the declaration for one who takes a גט from ארץ ישראל to overseas.

steps.title: Suggesting the argument depends on the reason for the declaration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא holds the reason for the declaration is that people overseas are not experts in writing לשמה. The other half of the suggestion comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One Sage holds the reason is that people overseas are not experts in writing a גט לשמה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to suggest that the תנא קמא and the חכמים argue about the reason for the declaration. This line gives the first half: the תנא קמא holds the reason is lack of expertise in לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is that scribes overseas do not know how to write לשמה, then a גט written in ארץ ישראל and taken overseas was written by experts. So there is no need for the declaration, which fits the תנא קמא. The second half, giving the reason of the חכמים, continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it that...?', a way the גמרא makes a suggestion
Experts, people who know the rules well

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of suggestion as in step 10, but there it was about רבן גמליאל. Here it is about the תנא קמא and the חכמים, and the case is someone taking a גט out of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: What, is it not this that they argue about?
That one Sage holds
phrases.notes: This 'one Sage' is the תנא קמא, the opinion we just saw in step 15.

phrases.english: the reason is that they are not experts in writing it for her sake,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument found in step 15 and suggests it depends on the two reasons for the declaration, the reasons of רבה and רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between the תנא קמא and the חכמים about one who takes a גט overseas depend on which reason for the declaration is correct?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not answered on this amud. The suggestion continues with the reason of the חכמים on the next amud.
